headline: Rate recovery lifts profit; guidance and capex plan raised
summary_short: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.53 versus $0.50 a year ago and GAAP EPS was $0.50 versus $0.45. CenterPoint raised 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.90-$1.92 and lifted its 10-year capital plan to $70.7B.
summary_long: Growth and rate recovery added $0.09 per share and weather and usage added $0.03, while O&M was flat. Higher financing costs from new debt and equity dilution subtracted $0.04, and other items subtracted $0.05, mainly the absence of last year's one-time tax optimization benefit. The 10-year capital plan rose $4.0B and $1.5B of investment moved into 2026-2030, supporting a rate base CAGR above 14%. 2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $2.07-$2.09 was initiated.
confidence_notes: Non-GAAP EPS is the company's own measure; no forward reconciliation is provided for guidance, per the release. The release read did not include a revenue line, so no revenue KPI is shown.

drivers.explanation: Growth and rate recovery added $0.09 per share and weather and usage $0.03, partly offset by $0.04 from higher financing expenses and $0.05 from other items, mainly last year's one-time tax benefit.
Raised to meet accelerating customer demand in the Greater Houston area, with another $1.5B of investment pulled into the first five years.
CEO points to Greater Houston growth opportunities and says discipline and a customer-driven approach support a tangible long-term growth plan.
